paper_title: A Short Proof of Bose--Einstein Condensation in the Gross--Pitaevskii Regime and Beyond (Brennecke, 2025, Annales Henri Poincare)
core_reasoning_1:
\textbf{Claim.}
Let \(\Pi_{\mathrm L}\) and \(\Pi_{\mathrm H}:=1-\Pi_{\mathrm L}\) be orthogonal projections on \(L^2(\Lambda^2)\), let
\[
H_2:=T+V_N,\qquad T:=-\Delta_{x_1}-\Delta_{x_2},\qquad D:=\Pi_{\mathrm H}H_2\Pi_{\mathrm H},
\]
and assume that \(D\) is strictly positive on \(\Pi_{\mathrm H}L^2(\Lambda^2)\). If
\[
V_{\mathrm{ren}}:=N^{1-\kappa}\left(V_N-V_N\Pi_{\mathrm H}D^{-1}\Pi_{\mathrm H}V_N\right),
\]
then every \(u\in L^2(\Lambda^2)\) satisfies
\[
\langle u,H_2u\rangle\geq
\left\langle \Pi_{\mathrm L}u,
\left(\Pi_{\mathrm L}T\Pi_{\mathrm L}+N^{\kappa-1}\Pi_{\mathrm L}V_{\mathrm{ren}}\Pi_{\mathrm L}\right)
\Pi_{\mathrm L}u\right\rangle .
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & \Pi_{\mathrm L}^2=\Pi_{\mathrm L}=\Pi_{\mathrm L}^\ast,\quad
       \Pi_{\mathrm H}:=1-\Pi_{\mathrm L},\quad
       \Pi_{\mathrm H}^2=\Pi_{\mathrm H}=\Pi_{\mathrm H}^\ast,\quad
       \Pi_{\mathrm L}\Pi_{\mathrm H}=0.\\[1mm]
(P2) & T\text{ is diagonal in the plane-wave basis defining }\Pi_{\mathrm L},\text{ hence }
       \Pi_{\mathrm L}T\Pi_{\mathrm H}=\Pi_{\mathrm H}T\Pi_{\mathrm L}=0.\\[1mm]
(P3) & H_2:=T+V_N,\quad
       A:=\Pi_{\mathrm L}H_2\Pi_{\mathrm L},\quad
       B:=\Pi_{\mathrm L}V_N\Pi_{\mathrm H},\quad
       D:=\Pi_{\mathrm H}H_2\Pi_{\mathrm H}.\\[1mm]
(P4) & D>0\text{ on }\Pi_{\mathrm H}L^2(\Lambda^2),\text{ so }D^{-1}\text{ and }D^{1/2}\text{ are well-defined there}.\\[1mm]
(P5) & V_{\mathrm{ren}}:=N^{1-\kappa}\left(V_N-V_N\Pi_{\mathrm H}D^{-1}\Pi_{\mathrm H}V_N\right).\\[1mm]
(P6) & \|D^{1/2}w\|^2\geq0\text{ for all }w\in\Pi_{\mathrm H}L^2(\Lambda^2).
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
Define the low- and high-momentum parts of \(u\) by
\begin{align}
u_{\mathrm L}&:=\Pi_{\mathrm L}u, & u_{\mathrm H}&:=\Pi_{\mathrm H}u .
\end{align}
Using the block decomposition from \((P1)\)--\((P3)\),
\begin{align}
\langle u,H_2u\rangle
&=\langle u_{\mathrm L},Au_{\mathrm L}\rangle
  +\langle u_{\mathrm L},Bu_{\mathrm H}\rangle
  +\langle u_{\mathrm H},B^\ast u_{\mathrm L}\rangle
  +\langle u_{\mathrm H},Du_{\mathrm H}\rangle \qquad \text{by }(P1)\text{--}(P3)\\
&=\langle u_{\mathrm L},(A-BD^{-1}B^\ast)u_{\mathrm L}\rangle
  +\langle u_{\mathrm H}+D^{-1}B^\ast u_{\mathrm L},
           D(u_{\mathrm H}+D^{-1}B^\ast u_{\mathrm L})\rangle
       \qquad \text{complete the square using }(P4)\\
&=\langle u_{\mathrm L},(A-BD^{-1}B^\ast)u_{\mathrm L}\rangle
  +\|D^{1/2}(u_{\mathrm H}+D^{-1}B^\ast u_{\mathrm L})\|^2
       \qquad \text{by }(P4)\\
&\geq\langle u_{\mathrm L},(A-BD^{-1}B^\ast)u_{\mathrm L}\rangle
       \qquad \text{by }(P6).
\end{align}
It remains to identify the Schur-complement operator on the low block:
\begin{align}
A-BD^{-1}B^\ast
&=\Pi_{\mathrm L}T\Pi_{\mathrm L}+\Pi_{\mathrm L}V_N\Pi_{\mathrm L}
  -\Pi_{\mathrm L}V_N\Pi_{\mathrm H}D^{-1}\Pi_{\mathrm H}V_N\Pi_{\mathrm L}
       \qquad \text{by }(P2),(P3)\\
&=\Pi_{\mathrm L}T\Pi_{\mathrm L}
  +\Pi_{\mathrm L}\left(V_N-V_N\Pi_{\mathrm H}D^{-1}\Pi_{\mathrm H}V_N\right)\Pi_{\mathrm L}
       \qquad \text{factor }\Pi_{\mathrm L}\text{ and }\Pi_{\mathrm H}\\
&=\Pi_{\mathrm L}T\Pi_{\mathrm L}+N^{\kappa-1}\Pi_{\mathrm L}V_{\mathrm{ren}}\Pi_{\mathrm L}
       \qquad \text{by }(P5).
\end{align}
Substituting this identity into the previous lower bound gives the announced inequality.

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{\langle u,H_2u\rangle\geq
\left\langle \Pi_{\mathrm L}u,
\left(\Pi_{\mathrm L}T\Pi_{\mathrm L}+N^{\kappa-1}\Pi_{\mathrm L}V_{\mathrm{ren}}\Pi_{\mathrm L}\right)
\Pi_{\mathrm L}u\right\rangle .}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_2:
\textbf{Claim.}
Let \(P_{\mathrm L}:=\{p\in\Lambda^\ast:|p|\leq N^\alpha\}\), with \(0\leq\alpha\leq1-\kappa\), and define
\[
\eta:=N^{1-\kappa}\Pi_{\mathrm H}\left[\Pi_{\mathrm H}(-\Delta_{x_1}-\Delta_{x_2}+V_N)\Pi_{\mathrm H}\right]^{-1}\Pi_{\mathrm H}V_N\Pi_{\mathrm L}.
\]
If \(p,q\in P_{\mathrm L}\), \(0<|r|<N^\delta\), \(\delta<\alpha\), and \(p+q-r\notin P_{\mathrm L}\), then the coefficient
\[
M_{pqr}:=\left\langle\varphi_{p+q-r}\otimes\varphi_r,
\eta\varphi_p\otimes\varphi_q\right\rangle
\]
satisfies
\[
|M_{pqr}|\leq C N^{-2\alpha},
\qquad
\max\{|p|,|q|\}>N^\alpha/3.
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & P_{\mathrm L}:=\{p\in\Lambda^\ast:|p|\leq N^\alpha\},\quad
       \Pi_{\mathrm H}=1-\Pi_{\mathrm L}\text{ on }L^2(\Lambda^2).\\[1mm]
(P2) & \eta=N^{1-\kappa}\Pi_{\mathrm H}\left[\Pi_{\mathrm H}(-\Delta_{x_1}-\Delta_{x_2}+V_N)\Pi_{\mathrm H}\right]^{-1}\Pi_{\mathrm H}V_N\Pi_{\mathrm L}.\\[1mm]
(P3) & \left|\left\langle\varphi_{k_1}\otimes\varphi_{k_2},
       \eta\varphi_{k_3}\otimes\varphi_{k_4}\right\rangle\right|
       \leq
       \dfrac{C\delta_{k_1+k_2,k_3+k_4}
       {\bf 1}_{(P_{\mathrm L}^2)^c}(k_1,k_2){\bf 1}_{P_{\mathrm L}^2}(k_3,k_4)}
       {|k_1|^2+|k_2|^2}.\\[3mm]
(P4) & p,q\in P_{\mathrm L},\quad 0<|r|<N^\delta,\quad \delta<\alpha,\quad p+q-r\notin P_{\mathrm L}.\\[1mm]
(P5) & \text{For }N\text{ large enough, }N^\alpha-N^\delta\geq 2N^\alpha/3.\\[1mm]
(P6) & \text{If }A+B>N^\alpha-N^\delta\text{ and }A,B\geq0,\text{ then }\max\{A,B\}>(N^\alpha-N^\delta)/2.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
First verify that the matrix element is in the support of the estimate \((P3)\):
\begin{align}
(p+q-r)+r&=p+q \qquad \text{algebra}\\
&=p+q \qquad \text{the incoming total momentum},\\
(p,q)&\in P_{\mathrm L}^2 \qquad \text{by }(P4),\\
(p+q-r,r)&\in (P_{\mathrm L}^2)^c \qquad \text{because }p+q-r\notin P_{\mathrm L}\text{ by }(P4).
\end{align}
Therefore \((P3)\), with \((k_1,k_2,k_3,k_4)=(p+q-r,r,p,q)\), gives
\begin{align}
|M_{pqr}|
&\leq \frac{C}{|p+q-r|^2+|r|^2} \qquad \text{by }(P3). 
\end{align}
Since \(p+q-r\notin P_{\mathrm L}\),
\begin{align}
|p+q-r|&>N^\alpha \qquad \text{by }(P1),(P4),\\
|p+q-r|^2+|r|^2&\geq |p+q-r|^2>N^{2\alpha} \qquad \text{square the previous inequality},\\
\frac{1}{|p+q-r|^2+|r|^2}&\leq N^{-2\alpha} \qquad \text{take reciprocals of positive numbers},\\
|M_{pqr}|&\leq C N^{-2\alpha} \qquad \text{substitute into the coefficient bound}.
\end{align}
It remains to show that one of the low incoming momenta must nevertheless be large. By the triangle inequality,
\begin{align}
N^\alpha
&<|p+q-r| \qquad \text{from }p+q-r\notin P_{\mathrm L}\\
&\leq |p|+|q|+|r| \qquad \text{triangle inequality},\\
|p|+|q|&>N^\alpha-|r|>N^\alpha-N^\delta \qquad \text{rearrange and use }|r|<N^\delta,\\
\max\{|p|,|q|\}&>\frac{N^\alpha-N^\delta}{2} \qquad \text{by }(P6),\\
\max\{|p|,|q|\}&>N^\alpha/3 \qquad \text{by }(P5).
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{|M_{pqr}|\leq C N^{-2\alpha}\quad\text{and}\quad\max\{|p|,|q|\}>N^\alpha/3.}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_3:
\textbf{Claim.}
Let \(\delta\in(\kappa/2,\alpha)\). With
\[
c_r:=a_r+d_r,
\qquad
 d_r:=\frac{N^\kappa}{N}\sum_{(p,q)\in P_{\mathrm L}^2}
 \left\langle\varphi_{p+q-r}\otimes\varphi_r,\eta\varphi_p\otimes\varphi_q\right\rangle
 a_{p+q-r}^\ast a_pa_q,
\]
there is a self-adjoint \(E_\delta\) such that
\[
\sum_{r\in\Lambda^\ast_+}|r|^2c_r^\ast c_r
\geq4\pi^2(\mathcal N_{<N^\delta}-a_0^\ast a_0)+E_\delta
\]
and
\[
\pm E_\delta\leq C N^{\kappa+\delta/2-3\alpha/2-1}(\mathcal K+\mathcal N)\mathcal N_{>N^{\alpha/3}}.
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & \Lambda^\ast=2\pi\mathbb Z^3,\quad \Lambda^\ast_+:=\Lambda^\ast\setminus\{0\},\quad
       |r|^2\geq4\pi^2\text{ for }r\in\Lambda^\ast_+.\\[1mm]
(P2) & \mathcal N_{<N^\delta}-a_0^\ast a_0=
       \sum_{r\in\Lambda^\ast_+:0<|r|<N^\delta}a_r^\ast a_r.\\[1mm]
(P3) & c_r:=a_r+d_r\text{ with }d_r\text{ as in the claim},\quad c_r^\ast c_r\geq0,\quad d_r^\ast d_r\geq0.\\[1mm]
(P4) & \sum_{r\in\Lambda^\ast_+}|r|^2c_r^\ast c_r
       \geq\sum_{r\in\Lambda^\ast_+:0<|r|<N^\delta}4\pi^2c_r^\ast c_r.\\[1mm]
(P5) & \text{For }0<|r|<N^\delta,\text{ the expansion }c_r^\ast c_r-a_r^\ast a_r
       =d_r^\ast a_r+a_r^\ast d_r+d_r^\ast d_r\text{ holds.}\\[1mm]
(P6) & \text{For every }\xi\in L_s^2(\Lambda^N),\\
     & \left|\dfrac{N^\kappa}{N}\sum_{\substack{p,q,r\in\Lambda^\ast\,:\,0<|r|<N^\delta}}
       \left\langle\varphi_{p+q-r}\otimes\varphi_r,\eta\varphi_p\otimes\varphi_q\right\rangle
       \langle\xi,a_r^\ast a_{p+q-r}^\ast a_pa_q\xi\rangle\right|\\[1mm]
     & \qquad\leq C N^{\kappa+\delta/2-3\alpha/2-1}
       \langle\xi,(\mathcal K+\mathcal N)\mathcal N_{>N^{\alpha/3}}\xi\rangle.\\[2mm]
(P7) & \text{If }|\langle\xi,E\xi\rangle|\leq\langle\xi,F\xi\rangle\text{ for all }\xi,
       \text{ then }\pm E\leq F\text{ as quadratic forms.}
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
Start from the low part of the modified kinetic energy:
\begin{align}
\sum_{r\in\Lambda^\ast_+}|r|^2c_r^\ast c_r
&\geq\sum_{\substack{r\in\Lambda^\ast_+\\0<|r|<N^\delta}}4\pi^2c_r^\ast c_r
       \qquad \text{by }(P4)\\
&=4\pi^2\sum_{\substack{r\in\Lambda^\ast_+\\0<|r|<N^\delta}}a_r^\ast a_r
  +4\pi^2\sum_{\substack{r\in\Lambda^\ast_+\\0<|r|<N^\delta}}(d_r^\ast a_r+a_r^\ast d_r+d_r^\ast d_r)
       \qquad \text{by }(P5)\\
&\geq4\pi^2(\mathcal N_{<N^\delta}-a_0^\ast a_0)
  +4\pi^2\sum_{\substack{r\in\Lambda^\ast_+\\0<|r|<N^\delta}}(d_r^\ast a_r+a_r^\ast d_r)
       \qquad \text{by }(P2),(P3).
\end{align}
Define
\begin{align}
E_\delta&:=4\pi^2\sum_{\substack{r\in\Lambda^\ast_+\\0<|r|<N^\delta}}(d_r^\ast a_r+a_r^\ast d_r). 
\end{align}
Then \(E_\delta^\ast=E_\delta\), and substituting the definition of \(d_r\) gives
\begin{align}
\langle\xi,E_\delta\xi\rangle
&=4\pi^2\frac{N^\kappa}{N}
  \sum_{\substack{p,q,r\in\Lambda^\ast\,:\,0<|r|<N^\delta}}
  \left\langle\varphi_{p+q-r}\otimes\varphi_r,\eta\varphi_p\otimes\varphi_q\right\rangle
  \langle\xi,a_r^\ast a_{p+q-r}^\ast a_pa_q\xi\rangle+\mathrm{c.c.}
       \qquad \text{by }(P3)\\
\left|\langle\xi,E_\delta\xi\rangle\right|
&\leq C N^{\kappa+\delta/2-3\alpha/2-1}
       \langle\xi,(\mathcal K+\mathcal N)\mathcal N_{>N^{\alpha/3}}\xi\rangle
       \qquad \text{by }(P6).
\end{align}
Applying \((P7)\) to the last inequality yields the stated two-sided form bound on \(E_\delta\).

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{\sum_{r\in\Lambda^\ast_+}|r|^2c_r^\ast c_r
\geq4\pi^2(\mathcal N_{<N^\delta}-a_0^\ast a_0)+E_\delta,
\qquad
\pm E_\delta\leq C N^{\kappa+\delta/2-3\alpha/2-1}(\mathcal K+\mathcal N)\mathcal N_{>N^{\alpha/3}}.}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_5:
\textbf{Claim.}
Let \(\psi_N\) be the normalized ground state of \(H_N\), and let \(\beta\geq0\). If
\[
\mathcal N_{>N^\beta}:=\sum_{|p|>N^\beta}a_p^\ast a_p,
\qquad
\mathcal K:=\sum_{p\in\Lambda^\ast_+}|p|^2a_p^\ast a_p,
\]
then
\[
\langle\psi_N,\mathcal N_{>N^\beta}\psi_N\rangle\leq CN^{1+\kappa-2\beta}.
\]
Consequently, if \(2\beta>\kappa\), then \(\langle\psi_N,\mathcal N_{>N^\beta}\psi_N\rangle=o(N)\).

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & \mathcal N_{>N^\beta}:=\sum_{|p|>N^\beta}a_p^\ast a_p,
       \quad \mathcal K:=\sum_{p\in\Lambda^\ast_+}|p|^2a_p^\ast a_p.\\[1mm]
(P2) & |p|>N^\beta\Longrightarrow 1<N^{-2\beta}|p|^2.\\[1mm]
(P3) & \mathcal K\leq H_N\text{ as quadratic forms, because the interaction potential is non-negative}.\\[1mm]
(P4) & E_N:=\langle\psi_N,H_N\psi_N\rangle\leq CN^{1+\kappa}.\\[1mm]
(P5) & \|\psi_N\|=1.\\[1mm]
(P6) & N^s=o(N)\text{ as }N\to\infty\Longleftrightarrow s<1.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
First compare the high-momentum number operator with the kinetic energy:
\begin{align}
\mathcal N_{>N^\beta}
&=\sum_{|p|>N^\beta}a_p^\ast a_p \qquad \text{by }(P1)\\
&\leq N^{-2\beta}\sum_{|p|>N^\beta}|p|^2a_p^\ast a_p \qquad \text{by }(P2)\\
&\leq N^{-2\beta}\mathcal K \qquad \text{by }(P1)\\
&\leq N^{-2\beta}H_N \qquad \text{by }(P3).
\end{align}
Taking the expectation in \(\psi_N\) gives
\begin{align}
\langle\psi_N,\mathcal N_{>N^\beta}\psi_N\rangle
&\leq N^{-2\beta}\langle\psi_N,H_N\psi_N\rangle
       \qquad \text{expectation of the previous form inequality}\\
&=N^{-2\beta}E_N \qquad \text{by }(P4)\text{ and the definition of }E_N\\
&\leq CN^{1+\kappa-2\beta} \qquad \text{by }(P4).
\end{align}
If \(2\beta>\kappa\), then \(1+\kappa-2\beta<1\), and so
\begin{align}
CN^{1+\kappa-2\beta}&=o(N) \qquad \text{by }(P6),\\
\langle\psi_N,\mathcal N_{>N^\beta}\psi_N\rangle&=o(N) \qquad \text{by comparison}.
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{\langle\psi_N,\mathcal N_{>N^\beta}\psi_N\rangle\leq CN^{1+\kappa-2\beta},\quad\text{hence }2\beta>\kappa\Rightarrow\langle\psi_N,\mathcal N_{>N^\beta}\psi_N\rangle=o(N).}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_6:
\textbf{Claim.}
Let \(0\leq\kappa<1/20\). The parameter choices in the paper can be made so that every error power in the final lower bound is strictly smaller than \(N^1\), and hence the total error is \(o(N)\).

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & N^s=o(N)\text{ as }N\to\infty\Longleftrightarrow s<1.\\[1mm]
(P2) & \text{For }0<\kappa<1/20,\text{ choose }
       \alpha:=(1+\varepsilon)\dfrac{41}{10}\kappa,
       \quad \beta:=(1+\varepsilon)\dfrac52\kappa,\\
     & \text{where }\varepsilon>0\text{ is sufficiently small, and choose }
       \delta\text{ with }\kappa/2<\delta<\alpha.\\[2mm]
(P3) & \text{For }\kappa=0,\text{ choose }0<\beta<\delta<\alpha<1/5.\\[1mm]
(P4) & \text{The kinetic and renormalized-potential error powers are}\\
     & s_1:=1+\kappa-2\delta,\quad
       s_2:=1+3\kappa+\delta/2-7\alpha/2,
       \quad s_3:=5\kappa/2+\delta/2-\alpha,\\
     & s_4:=1+2\kappa-2\alpha,
       \quad s_5:=\kappa+3\alpha.\\[1mm]
(P5) & \text{The three-body error powers are}\\
     & t_1:=1+5\kappa-2\beta,
       \quad t_2:=1/2+9\kappa/2+5\alpha/2-2\beta,\\
     & t_3:=1+9\kappa/2+\beta/2-3\alpha/2,
       \quad t_4:=1/2+4\kappa+\alpha+\beta/2,\\
     & t_5:=1+4\kappa+5\beta/2-5\alpha/2.\\[1mm]
(P6) & \text{If inequalities are strict at }\varepsilon=0\text{ and depend continuously on }\varepsilon,
       \text{ then they remain strict for sufficiently small }\varepsilon>0.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
First consider \(0<\kappa<1/20\). Since \(\delta\in(\kappa/2,\alpha)\), choose it close enough to \(\kappa/2\) that the following strict inequalities persist. At \(\varepsilon=0\) and \(\delta=\kappa/2\),
\begin{align}
s_1&=1+\kappa-2(\kappa/2)=1 \qquad \text{boundary value; choosing }\delta>\kappa/2\text{ gives }s_1<1,\\
s_2&=1+3\kappa+\kappa/4-\frac72\cdot\frac{41}{10}\kappa
    =1-\frac{111}{10}\kappa<1,\\
s_3&=\frac52\kappa+\frac14\kappa-\frac{41}{10}\kappa
    =-\frac{27}{20}\kappa<1,\\
s_4&=1+2\kappa-2\cdot\frac{41}{10}\kappa
    =1-\frac{31}{5}\kappa<1,\\
s_5&=\kappa+3\cdot\frac{41}{10}\kappa
    =\frac{133}{10}\kappa<1
    \qquad \text{because }\kappa<1/20.
\end{align}
For the three-body powers, substitute \(\alpha=(41/10)\kappa\) and \(\beta=(5/2)\kappa\) at \(\varepsilon=0\):
\begin{align}
t_1&=1+5\kappa-2\cdot\frac52\kappa=1,\qquad
       \text{and }\varepsilon>0\text{ makes }t_1=1-5\varepsilon\kappa<1,\\
t_2&=\frac12+\frac92\kappa+\frac52\cdot\frac{41}{10}\kappa-2\cdot\frac52\kappa
    =\frac12+\frac{39}{4}\kappa<1
    \qquad \text{because }\kappa<\frac{2}{39},\\
t_3&=1+\frac92\kappa+\frac12\cdot\frac52\kappa-\frac32\cdot\frac{41}{10}\kappa
    =1-\frac25\kappa<1,\\
t_4&=\frac12+4\kappa+\frac{41}{10}\kappa+\frac12\cdot\frac52\kappa
    =\frac12+\frac{187}{20}\kappa<1
    \qquad \text{because }\kappa<\frac{10}{187},\\
t_5&=1+4\kappa+\frac52\cdot\frac52\kappa-\frac52\cdot\frac{41}{10}\kappa
    =1-\frac12\kappa<1.
\end{align}
The strict inequalities other than the boundary cases remain true for sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\) by \((P6)\), and the two boundary cases \(s_1,t_1\) are made strict by \(\delta>\kappa/2\) and \(\varepsilon>0\), respectively. Thus all powers are below \(1\) when \(0<\kappa<1/20\). For \(\kappa=0\), using \((P3)\),
\begin{align}
s_1&=1-2\delta<1,&
 s_2&=1+\delta/2-7\alpha/2<1,&
 s_3&=\delta/2-\alpha<1,\\
s_4&=1-2\alpha<1,&
 s_5&=3\alpha<1,&
 t_1&=1-2\beta<1,\\
t_2&=1/2+5\alpha/2-2\beta<1,&
 t_3&=1+\beta/2-3\alpha/2<1,&
 t_4&=1/2+\alpha+\beta/2<1,\\
t_5&=1+5\beta/2-5\alpha/2<1,
\end{align}
where the restrictions follow by taking \(0<\beta<\delta<\alpha<1/5\) sufficiently separated. Therefore \((P1)\) implies that each corresponding power of \(N\) is \(o(N)\).

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{0\leq\kappa<1/20\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
N^{s_j}=o(N)\ (1\leq j\leq5),\qquad N^{t_j}=o(N)\ (1\leq j\leq5).}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_7:
\textbf{Claim.}
For \(0\leq\kappa<1/20\), the ground state \(\psi_N\) of \(H_N\) satisfies
\[
\lim_{N\to\infty}\langle\varphi_0,\gamma_N^{(1)}\varphi_0\rangle=1.
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & E_N:=\langle\psi_N,H_N\psi_N\rangle,
       \quad \|\psi_N\|=1,
       \quad E_N\leq4\pi aN^{1+\kappa}+o(N).\\[1mm]
(P2) & \text{The many-body Schur-complement lower bound is}\\
     & \quad H_N\geq
       \sum_{r\in\Lambda^\ast_+}|r|^2c_r^\ast c_r+
       \mathcal W_{\mathrm{ren}}-R_N.\\[1mm]
(P3) & \text{In the ground state and for }0\leq\kappa<1/20,\\
     & \quad \left\langle\psi_N,
       \sum_{r\in\Lambda^\ast_+}|r|^2c_r^\ast c_r\psi_N\right\rangle
       \geq4\pi^2\langle\psi_N,\mathcal N_+\psi_N\rangle+o(N).\\[2mm]
(P4) & \text{In the ground state and for }0\leq\kappa<1/20,\\
     & \quad \langle\psi_N,\mathcal W_{\mathrm{ren}}\psi_N\rangle
       \geq4\pi aN^{1+\kappa}+o(N).\\[1mm]
(P5) & \text{In the ground state and for }0\leq\kappa<1/20,\quad
       |\langle\psi_N,R_N\psi_N\rangle|=o(N).\\[1mm]
(P6) & \mathcal N_+:=\sum_{r\in\Lambda^\ast\setminus\{0\}}a_r^\ast a_r\geq0.\\[1mm]
(P7) & 1-\langle\varphi_0,\gamma_N^{(1)}\varphi_0\rangle
       =N^{-1}\langle\psi_N,\mathcal N_+\psi_N\rangle.\\[1mm]
(P8) & \text{If }0\leq x_N\leq o(N),\text{ then }N^{-1}x_N\to0.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
Take the expectation of the many-body lower bound in the ground state:
\begin{align}
E_N
&=\langle\psi_N,H_N\psi_N\rangle \qquad \text{by }(P1)\\
&\geq
\left\langle\psi_N,\sum_{r\in\Lambda^\ast_+}|r|^2c_r^\ast c_r\psi_N\right\rangle
+\langle\psi_N,\mathcal W_{\mathrm{ren}}\psi_N\rangle
-\langle\psi_N,R_N\psi_N\rangle
\qquad \text{by }(P2)\\
&\geq4\pi^2\langle\psi_N,\mathcal N_+\psi_N\rangle
+4\pi aN^{1+\kappa}+o(N)
\qquad \text{by }(P3),(P4),(P5).
\end{align}
Compare this lower bound with the upper bound on \(E_N\):
\begin{align}
4\pi aN^{1+\kappa}+o(N)
&\geq E_N \qquad \text{by }(P1)\\
&\geq4\pi aN^{1+\kappa}+4\pi^2\langle\psi_N,\mathcal N_+\psi_N\rangle+o(N)\\
4\pi^2\langle\psi_N,\mathcal N_+\psi_N\rangle
&\leq o(N) \qquad \text{subtract }4\pi aN^{1+\kappa},\\
\langle\psi_N,\mathcal N_+\psi_N\rangle&=o(N) \qquad \text{by }(P6).
\end{align}
Finally use the exact relation between depletion and the reduced density matrix:
\begin{align}
1-\langle\varphi_0,\gamma_N^{(1)}\varphi_0\rangle
&=N^{-1}\langle\psi_N,\mathcal N_+\psi_N\rangle
       \qquad \text{by }(P7)\\
&\longrightarrow0 \qquad \text{by }(P8),\\
\lim_{N\to\infty}\langle\varphi_0,\gamma_N^{(1)}\varphi_0\rangle&=1.
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{\lim_{N\to\infty}\langle\varphi_0,\gamma_N^{(1)}\varphi_0\rangle=1.}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
